title: White Ash: Ancient White Ashes You Can Visit
meta_description: A North American ash now under attack from the emerald ash borer. Atlanta's Georgia champion, 40.6 metres tall, leans over a BeltLine path.
intro: The white ash is a North American ash under attack at home from the emerald ash borer, an invasive beetle that has killed tens of millions of ash trees across the continent. NYC Parks calls the one by the Bedford Park gate of the New York Botanical Garden a rare survivor of the borer; the garden's records say it was donated in 1907, while Parks also calls it a forest remnant. The widest we map, in the Bronx's Van Cortlandt Park, is nearly 4.8 metres round. In Atlanta the Georgia champion, 40.6 metres tall, leans over a BeltLine path, already struck by lightning and found by the borer. Two grow in Europe. One stands outside the forest shop at Bucaco in Portugal, planted around 1880 by the register's count, and the other on Munich's Maximiliansplatz, protected by a city ordinance that calls the species rare there.
